Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 10605 of 2023

Applicant :- Shiv Kumar Awasthi And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Pankaj Kumar Tripathi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pankaj Dwivedi
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned brief holder for the State apprised the Court that he has received instructions in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be disposed of on merit.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicants is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Pankaj Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Pankaj Dwivedi, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned brief holder for the State.
4.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 345 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Etmaddaula, District Agra, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged against applicants on 05.07.2023 and according to the FIR,

applicant no. 1 is the younger brother of the informant and applicant no. 2 is his wife and they prepared a forged power of attorney and on the basis of forged power of attorney, they got executed a sale deed in their favour, however, mother of the applicant no. 1 and informant was the owner of the property and on the basis of her Will, informant got possession over the property.
6. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted on the basis of false allegation, applicants have been made accused in the present matter and original allottee Chetan Das executed power of attorney in favour of the applicant no. 1 and on the basis of power of attorney, the sale deeds were executed and no fraud has been committed by the applicants.
7.

He further submitted that informant, who was elder brother of applicant no. 1, was continuously trying to grab the property in question and in the year 2022, applicant no.1 filed a declarity civil suit against him as case no. 1278 of 2022 to declare him real owner of the property in question and the plaint of the same has been annexed as Annexure No. 3 to the affidavit.
He further submitted that when informant came to know about this fact then in the year 2023 he filed FIR of the present case.
8. He further submitted that present dispute appears to be civil dispute and no criminal liability is fastened against thee applicants.

He further submitted that in the year 2016, informant also lodged a criminal complaint against the applicants, which is still pending and criminal complaint lodged by the informant has been annexed alongwith the rejoinder affidavit.

9. He further submitted that applicants are not having any criminal history and police is continuously trying to arrest them, therefore, considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, applicants may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
10.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant however, opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that even before lodgement of the FIR of the present case, applicant no. 1 had filed a civil suit against the informant in the year 2022 with regard to the property in question, which is still pending.
11. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

12. Considering the fact that present dispute appears to be civil dispute and with regard to the same dispute, a civil suit has been filed by applicant no. 1 against informant, which is still pending and after lodgement of the civil suit, the FIR of the present case was lodged, in my view applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

14. In the event of arrest of the applicants, Shiv Kumar Awasthi and Smt. Sunita Devi involved in the aforesaid case crime number, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of trial on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Shiv Kumar Awasthi And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118443225/

Presiding Officer/Court Concerned, with the conditions that:-
i. that the applicants shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

16. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
